newsitem.title: BANGLADESH: Bangladesh calls bidding for drilling of gas, oil.
newsitem.headline: Bangladesh calls bidding for drilling of gas, oil.

text.p: Bangladesh has called for international gas and oil exploration bids and energy officials said on Friday they expect a good response after Cairn Energy Plc struck huge reserves in the Bay of Bengal.
The officials said Bangladesh had set March 24 for bidding in London and March 31 in Houston, Texas.
They said the biddings in London and Houston would be for 15 blocks after the government had already offered eight blocks to foreign firms.
"We hope no less than 80 leading oil companies will participate in the biddings," an official with Petrobangla, the state-owned oil and gas corporation, said on Friday.
He said United Meridian Corp had entered into a production sharing contract with Petrobangla early this month for exploration in a block in the southeastern Chittagong Hill Tracts.

The company plans to dig its first exploration well next winter and officials said there was a greater possibility of finding oil reserves in the rugged hills, the area deserted by Royal/Dutch Shell Group in the 1980s.
But Shell is returning now with a massive investment of $2.5 billion in a project to convert natural gas into petroleum products. It has also proposed to invest in a power generation unit.
"The success of Cairn Energy (in striking gas in the Bay) and a package of lucrative incentives have been attracting leading oil firms around the world," another official told Reuters.

Richard Heaton, general manager of Britain's Cairn Energy in Bangladesh, said his company would soon begin appraisal drilling of the Sangu-3 and Sangu-4 wells, and in two more wells in the area where it found gas last year.
It has already drilled the Sangu-1 and Sangu-2 wells.
"The gas will be flowing to Chittagong town in April 1998," Richard told Reuters on Thursday.

He said approximate gas reserves in the Sangu field were about one trillion cubic feet. Cairn Energy signed a gas purchase and sale agreement with Petrobangla during British Prime Minister John Major's visit to Bangladesh in January.
Richard said the company had already spent $40 million and the total investment might reach $200 million when it completed drilling in the Sangu gas field.
Britain's Prince Charles, now on a visit to Bangladesh, flew to Cairn's gas rig in the Bay of Bengal on Friday.

Energy ministry sources said Unocal Corp, which has already teamed up with Occidental Corp to drill for gas in a known reserve in northeastern Sylhet, had been awarded a deal for development of southern Bhola gas field discovered by Petrobangla in 1994.
The Bhola gas field has a reserve of 0.4 trillion cubic feet of gas, they said. Unocal would also set up a coal-fired power plant in Bangladesh's northern region.
The sources hinted the government was also planning to privatise the exploration and development wing of Petrobangla, "attracting more investment, speeding up of handling and solving problems".
